pr.title: Sanitize non-finite range coordinates in Diagnostic.from
pr.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.

Fixes #177094

### Problem

Diagnostics with non-finite range coordinates (`NaN`, `Infinity`) are passed through `Diagnostic.from` into `IMarkerData` unchanged. When marshalled across the RPC boundary to the main thread (and onward to LSP language servers), `NaN` is serialized as JSON `null`, which violates the LSP spec (uinteger required) and causes downstream language servers to fail when handling code action requests.

The original report shows the malformed payload:

```json
"start": { "line": null, "character": 0 }
```

This is the case @jrieken called out in [#177094 (comment)](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/177094#issuecomment-1472228867): *"diagnostics are created for ill-formed ranges (nan, null, -1) and our validation doesn't catch all of them ... anyone is invited to improve range validation."*

### Fix

After converting `value.range` via `Range.from(...)`, replace only non-finite coordinates. Non-finite start coordinates fall back to `1`; non-finite end coordinates fall back to the corresponding sanitized start coordinate. Then clamp the end position so it cannot precede the start, preserving the remaining finite coordinates wherever possible. The diagnostic is preserved (extension authors still see their message in the Problems view) and downstream consumers + LSP clients receive a finite, ordered range.

Scope is intentionally narrow: only the diagnostic conversion path. `Range.from` itself is unchanged, and other call sites (location, document symbol, etc.) are unaffected.

### Tests

Added a `Diagnostic` suite to `extHostTypeConverters.test.ts` with explicit equality assertions for all four 1-based coordinates:
- Well-formed range remains `(3,5)-(7,9)`, and its diagnostic message is preserved.
- Non-finite start and end lines fall back to `(1,1)-(1,1)`.
- A single NaN column preserves the finite line and column, producing `(3,6)-(3,6)`.
- A non-finite end falls back to the finite start at `(6,4)-(6,4)` without inverting the range.
- An infinite end line is sanitized to `(1,1)-(1,1)`.

Focused test command on Windows:

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\common\extHostTypeConverters.test.ts --grep "extHostTypeConverters Diagnostic"
```

Not rerun for this documentation-only follow-up: the isolated checkout lacks its build/test dependencies, and approval to install them was unavailable. The current implementation and exact-value assertions were verified against both review comments.

Adds sanitization for `Diagnostic` range coordinates to prevent non-finite values (NaN/Infinity) from producing invalid JSON/LSP requests, and introduces regression tests to validate the converter behavior.

- Add unit tests covering well-formed ranges and NaN/Infinity edge cases for diagnostics.

commit.message:
Sanitize non-finite range coordinates in Diagnostic.from

Diagnostics whose range contains non-finite numbers (NaN, Infinity) currently
flow through to IMarkerData unchanged. When marshalled across the RPC
boundary, NaN is serialized as JSON null, which breaks LSP code action
requests (the spec requires uinteger line/character values).

Sanitize the converted range in Diagnostic.from: if any of the four
coordinates is non-finite, replace the range with a known-good (1,1,1,1)
default so downstream IMarkerData consumers and LSP clients receive a
valid range.

Fixes #177094

Sanitize Diagnostic range coordinates per-axis without inverting

Replace only the non-finite coordinates instead of resetting the whole range, so valid line/character values are preserved. Derive the end fallback from the sanitized start and clamp it so the end can never precede the start on either axis.

Tests assert the exact sanitized coordinates and cover a non-finite end that would otherwise invert a finite start.

Merge main into fix/validate-diagnostic-range

Resolve test merge conflicts for #318520 while preserving both branches' tests.
